comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C16, C18-C20, C60 regarding UPS-mediated degradation of nsp16. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and internal consistency; peer reviewers explicitly state 'the experimental approach looks convincing' and treat the data as foundational.

Perfect agreement on claims C26-C29, C71-C72 regarding ubiquitination and linkage specificity (K27 and K48). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing. OpenEval notes strong evidence from single-lysine ubiquitin mutants; peer reviewers explicitly endorse the K48- and K27-linkage findings as 'convincing.'

Perfect agreement on claims C30-C34 regarding E3 ligase interactions and ER localization. Both evaluations accept the Co-IP, FRET, and immunofluorescence data without concerns. OpenEval highlights FRET as strong evidence for direct interaction; peer reviewers accept all interaction data as part of the 'convincing' overall support.

Perfect agreement on claims C35-C39 regarding domain mapping for UBR5 and MARCHF7. Both evaluations find the experimental design appropriate for separating binding from catalytic activity. OpenEval notes systematic approach; peer reviewers affirm the overall experimental approach as 'convincing.'

Perfect agreement on claims C40-C43 regarding antiviral effects. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing across multiple readouts (viral mRNA, titers, protein levels). OpenEval highlights use of two viral strains and statistical significance; peer reviewers affirm mechanisms 'effectively inhibiting SARS-CoV-2 replication.'

Perfect agreement on claims C44-C46 regarding gain-of-function effects. Both evaluations accept the rescue experiments and negative controls with catalytically inactive mutants. OpenEval notes potential transfection efficiency concerns but overall supports claims; peer reviewers treat data as confirmatory without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C47-C48, C74 regarding broad-spectrum activity across viral variants. Both evaluations endorse the findings. OpenEval notes degradation occurs 'to varying degrees' suggesting some resistance; peer reviewers treat variant data as a strength without raising concerns about variability.

Divergent evaluations on claims C49-C52 regarding expression dynamics and patient data. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small patient sample size, lack of statistical significance for MARCHF7, and use of PBMCs rather than lung tissue. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED without questioning these limitations, treating data as supporting biological relevance.

Perfect agreement on claims C53-C56 regarding in vivo antiviral effects. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing. OpenEval acknowledges limitations of delivery method and small sample size (n=3) but supports claims; peer reviewers explicitly endorse in vivo studies as 'a strength' with 'ok' controls.

Perfect agreement on claims C66-C67 regarding ubiquitination site mapping. Both evaluations accept the MS identification and mutagenesis validation. OpenEval notes appropriate interpretation that K76R reduces but doesn't eliminate ubiquitination; peer reviewers accept data without critique.

Perfect agreement on claims C70, C73 representing main conclusions. Both evaluations strongly support these high-level summary statements. OpenEval notes they are well-supported by totality of evidence; peer reviewers describe work as 'important' with 'convincing' support for overall claims.

Strong agreement on claims C23-C25 regarding independent E3 ligase action and domain requirements. OpenEval evaluates C23-C25 as SUPPORTED with strong evidence from epistasis and catalytically inactive mutants. Peer R2 evaluates C22-C25 as SUPPORTED, affirming identification of E3 ligases and finding experimental approach 'convincing.'

Partial overlap on claim C21 regarding MS-based identification of nsp16 interactors. OpenEval evaluates C21-C22 as SUPPORTED but notes missing MS data quality metrics and statistical thresholds. Peer R12 evaluates only C21 as SUPPORTED without questioning bioinformatics methodology.

Partial overlap on claim C22 regarding KEGG/GO analysis. OpenEval evaluates C21-C22 together as SUPPORTED with caveat about missing MS quality metrics. Peer R2 evaluates C22-C25 together as SUPPORTED, focusing on E3 ligase identification rather than bioinformatics details.

Perfect agreement on claims C1-C9 regarding SARS-CoV-2 background. Both evaluations find these background claims SUPPORTED by appropriate citations and consistent with established knowledge. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C10-C15 regarding UPS and E3 ligase background. Both evaluations find these background claims SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. OpenEval notes they establish conceptual framework; peer reviewers treat as established knowledge without concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C57-C65 regarding nsp16 structural studies and E3 ligase background. Both evaluations find these background claims SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. OpenEval notes they establish novelty of studying UBR5 and MARCHF7; peer reviewers accept without concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C68-C69 regarding in vivo delivery method context. Both evaluations find these background claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes authors appropriately acknowledge limitations; peer reviewers accept as relevant context without concerns.

Perfect agreement on claim C17 regarding rationale for focusing on nsp16 over nsp8. Both evaluations find this background claim SUPPORTED by appropriate citation. No concerns raised by either evaluation.
